nodes.label: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
nodes.rationale: Proposes Verbalized Sampling (VS) method to mitigate mode collapse in LLMs by having models verbalize probability distributions alongside generated responses, enabling sampling from diverse pre-training distributions rather than collapsed modes.

nodes.label: Mode Collapse in LLMs
nodes.rationale: Central problem addressed: aligned LLMs tend to concentrate probability mass on a narrow set of high-frequency outputs, losing diversity from pre-training. VS aims to recover this lost diversity.

nodes.label: VS-Standard Method
nodes.rationale: Core variant of Verbalized Sampling where models generate k candidate responses with explicit probability annotations relative to full distribution.

nodes.label: VS-Multi Method
nodes.rationale: Multi-turn variant of VS where model generates candidates across multiple API calls, each with probability annotations, enabling iterative refinement.

nodes.label: Direct Prompting Baseline
nodes.rationale: Standard baseline where model generates single response per call; exhibits severe mode collapse with probability mass concentrated on few high-frequency outputs.

nodes.label: Sequence Prompting Baseline
nodes.rationale: Baseline where model generates k responses in list format without probability annotations; produces uniform distribution missing peaked structure of ground truth.

nodes.label: KL Divergence Metric
nodes.rationale: Primary metric used to quantify alignment between model output distributions and ground-truth pre-training distributions; lower values indicate better alignment.

nodes.label: RedPajama Corpus
nodes.rationale: Large-scale English corpus (~900M web documents) used as proxy for pre-training distribution to evaluate whether VS recovers ground-truth distributions.

nodes.label: GPT-4.1 Model
nodes.rationale: Primary proprietary model evaluated in experiments; shows VS-Standard achieves 0.132 KL divergence vs 14.886 for Direct prompting on pre-training distribution.

nodes.label: Claude-4-Sonnet Model
nodes.rationale: Secondary proprietary model evaluated; shows similar pattern with VS-Standard achieving 0.122 KL divergence vs 16.160 for Direct prompting.

nodes.label: Poem Generation Task
nodes.rationale: Creative writing task used to evaluate diversity; VS-Standard achieves 20.7±5.7 diversity vs 11.1±1.0 for Direct prompting.

nodes.label: Joke Generation Task
nodes.rationale: Creative writing task; VS-Standard achieves 60.0±2.4 diversity vs 22.3±4.5 for Direct prompting, demonstrating strong mitigation of mode collapse.

nodes.label: Story Generation Task
nodes.rationale: Creative writing task; VS-Standard achieves 32.4±6.2 diversity vs 23.0±4.5 for Direct prompting.

nodes.label: Open-Ended QA Task
nodes.rationale: Constrained answer space task (US states, countries, programming languages) used to evaluate coverage and precision of VS methods.

nodes.label: Verbalized Probability Calibration Study
nodes.rationale: Evaluates whether verbalized probabilities contain meaningful distributional information; shows Pearson r=0.741 for US states, indicating rank-order preservation.

nodes.label: Probability Threshold Tuning
nodes.rationale: Mechanism to control diversity by instructing model to sample from tail distribution with probability < p%; enables fine-grained diversity control through prompting.

nodes.label: Temperature Ablation Study
nodes.rationale: Evaluates interaction between VS and temperature parameter; shows VS-Standard maintains superior Pareto front across temperature values 0.4-1.4.

nodes.label: Top-p Sampling Ablation Study
nodes.rationale: Shows synergistic relationship where both quality and diversity increase as p rises from 0.7 to ~0.95; VS-Standard achieves superior Pareto front.

nodes.label: Min-p Sampling Ablation Study
nodes.rationale: Evaluates VS with min-p sampling on open-source models; VS-Standard maintains exceptionally high quality even at diversity levels causing collapse in baselines.

nodes.label: Cost-Efficiency Analysis
nodes.rationale: VS-Standard incurs 1.12× cost overhead vs Direct but achieves 1.86× diversity gain; favorable trade-off for applications prioritizing diversity.

nodes.label: RLHF Post-Training Stages
nodes.rationale: Ablation across SFT, RLHF, RLVR stages shows VS maintains ~30% diversity while Direct drops from 20.8% to 10.8%, demonstrating mitigation of alignment-induced collapse.

nodes.label: Tulu-3 Model Family
nodes.rationale: Open-source model family with checkpoints at different post-training stages used to empirically demonstrate mode collapse and VS effectiveness.

nodes.author: Jiayi Zhang, Simon Yu, Derek Chong, Anthony Sicilia, Michael R. Tomz, Christopher D. Manning, Weiyan Shi
nodes.rationale: Addresses mode collapse in LLMs through data-centric analysis of typicality bias and proposes training-free inference-time remedy

nodes.label: Mode Collapse
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where post-training alignment reduces LLM diversity, causing models to favor narrow set of responses

nodes.label: Typicality Bias
nodes.rationale: Human tendency to prefer familiar, fluent, predictable text; identified as fundamental data-level driver of mode collapse

nodes.label: Verbalized Sampling (VS)
nodes.rationale: Training-free prompting strategy that asks model to verbalize probability distribution over responses instead of single instance

nodes.label: Cognitive Psychology Foundations of Typicality
nodes.rationale: Mere-exposure effect, availability heuristic, processing fluency, and schema congruity theory establish psychological basis for typicality preference

nodes.label: HelpSteer Preference Dataset
nodes.rationale: Human-annotated preference dataset used to empirically verify typicality bias in preference data

nodes.label: Llama-3.1-405B
nodes.rationale: Base model used as reference for computing log-probability as typicality proxy

nodes.label: GLM-4.5
nodes.rationale: Base model used as reference for computing log-probability as typicality proxy

nodes.label: Bradley-Terry Model
nodes.rationale: Statistical model used to decompose reward into true task utility and typicality bias components

nodes.label: Creative Writing Task
nodes.rationale: Application domain including poem, joke, and story generation where VS shows 1.6-2.1× diversity improvement

nodes.label: Social Dialogue Simulation
nodes.rationale: Application domain where VS induces more human-like behaviors in dialogue generation

nodes.label: Synthetic Data Generation
nodes.rationale: Application domain where VS generates more diverse synthetic data improving downstream task performance

nodes.label: Open-Ended Question Answering
nodes.rationale: Application domain with multiple valid answers where VS generates broader response distributions

nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
nodes.rationale: Post-training alignment method that can unintentionally cause mode collapse through KL-regularized optimization

nodes.label: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
nodes.rationale: Training method that can lead to overfitting and limited diversity due to cross-entropy loss function

nodes.label: μ-sampling
nodes.rationale: Decoding strategy for improving diversity; computationally expensive alternative to VS

nodes.label: Mirostat
nodes.rationale: Decoding technique for improving diversity by regulating text perplexity

nodes.label: Min-p Sampling
nodes.rationale: Decoding technique for improving diversity; restricted to open-source models

nodes.label: Mere-Exposure Effect
nodes.rationale: Cognitive psychology principle that frequent or easily recalled content is perceived as more preferable

nodes.label: Availability Heuristic
nodes.rationale: Cognitive bias where easily recalled content is perceived as more likely and preferable

nodes.label: Processing Fluency
nodes.rationale: Cognitive principle that easy-to-process content is perceived as more truthful and higher-quality

nodes.label: Schema Congruity Theory
nodes.rationale: Theory indicating content aligned with existing mental models receives less critical scrutiny

nodes.label: Output Diversity Metric
nodes.rationale: Primary evaluation metric showing VS achieves 1.6-2.1× improvement in creative writing and recovers 66.8% of base model diversity

nodes.label: Human Evaluation Score
nodes.rationale: Evaluation metric showing VS improves human evaluation scores by 25.7% in creative writing

nodes.label: Quality-Diversity Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Central finding that VS systematically improves diversity without sacrificing quality, factual accuracy, or safety

nodes.label: Inference-Time Remedy
nodes.rationale: VS operates at inference time without requiring model retraining, making it broadly applicable

nodes.label: Data-Centric Perspective on Mode Collapse
nodes.rationale: Novel theoretical framework attributing mode collapse to data-level bias rather than purely algorithmic causes

nodes.label: Typicality Bias in RLHF
nodes.rationale: Cognitive tendency of human annotators to prefer conventional responses, causing mode collapse in aligned LLMs through preference data

nodes.label: Mode Collapse in Aligned LLMs
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where probability mass concentrates toward typical completions favored by reference policy when rewards are flat

nodes.label: Verbalized Sampling (VS)
nodes.rationale: Training-free prompting method that frames requests as sampling from distributions rather than single instances to restore diversity

nodes.label: Semantic Diversity Metric
nodes.rationale: Calculated as 1 minus mean pairwise cosine similarity of response embeddings

nodes.label: Emergent Trend: Larger Models Benefit More
nodes.rationale: Larger models achieve diversity gains 1.5 to 2 times greater than smaller models with VS

nodes.label: Cognitive Burden Effect
nodes.rationale: Complex prompts can degrade LLM performance, but VS variants overcome this effect

nodes.label: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
nodes.author: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning, Shi
nodes.rationale: Core research paper proposing Verbalized Sampling as a method to mitigate mode collapse in LLMs by leveraging the representativeness heuristic

nodes.label: Mode Collapse in LLMs
nodes.rationale: Central problem: RLHF and preference optimization amplify typicality bias, causing models to collapse to prototypical responses and lose diversity

nodes.label: Typicality Bias in Preference Data
nodes.rationale: Empirical finding: base models systematically prefer higher-probability (more typical) responses; this bias is preserved through instruction tuning and varies by demographic group

nodes.label: Representativeness Heuristic
nodes.author: Tversky & Kahneman (1974)
nodes.rationale: Cognitive psychology principle: humans and LLMs judge outcomes as typical if they appear representative of the generating process, not by actual probability

nodes.label: Verbalized Sampling (VS)
nodes.rationale: Proposed method: shift from instance-level prompts to distribution-level prompts where models generate k candidates with verbalized probabilities, exploiting representativeness to recover diversity

nodes.label: Theorem D.1: Instance-Level Collapse
nodes.rationale: Formal result: under flat rewards and power-transform sharpening (γ>1), instance prompts collapse to the single mode of the reference distribution exponentially fast

nodes.label: Theorem D.2: List-Level Collapse
nodes.rationale: Formal result: list prompts collapse to top-k modes with at most uniform diversity over k items; auto-regressive conditioning amplifies collapse at each step

nodes.label: Theorem D.4: Diversity Recovery via Representativeness
nodes.rationale: Core theoretical contribution: distribution-level prompts with representativeness preference recover diversity by concentrating on high-entropy typical-set distributions

nodes.label: Theorem D.7: Typical Set Concentration
nodes.rationale: Information-theoretic result: under model-side representativeness assumption, sharpened policy concentrates on typical-set sequences (high-entropy, diverse)

nodes.label: Assumption D.3: Representativeness Preference
nodes.rationale: Weak assumption: humans prefer representative distributions with probability >0.5; deliberately weak to allow for noise and calibration uncertainty

nodes.label: Assumption D.6: Model-Side Representativeness
nodes.rationale: Assumption: pre-trained models assign higher likelihood to typical-set (diverse) sequences than degenerate (repetitive) ones under VS prompts

nodes.label: Creative Writing Experiments
nodes.rationale: Evaluation on poem, story, and joke generation; VS achieves 30-50% higher diversity while maintaining comparable quality across 9 models

nodes.label: Dialogue Simulation Experiments
nodes.rationale: Evaluation on donation amount alignment; VS achieves Pareto optimality with both higher linguistic diversity and better distribution alignment (KS test)

nodes.label: Open-Ended Question Answering
nodes.rationale: Evaluation on CoverageQA; VS improves coverage of valid answers and reduces KL divergence from pretraining distribution without sacrificing precision

nodes.label: Commonsense Reasoning (SimpleQA)
nodes.rationale: Evaluation on factual accuracy; VS-CoT achieves best Top@1 and Pass@N accuracy, confirming diversity gains do not compromise factual correctness

nodes.label: Synthetic Data Generation
nodes.rationale: Positive and negative data generation; VS improves downstream model performance when used for finetuning and offline RL

nodes.label: Random Number Generation (Dice Roll)
nodes.rationale: Evaluation on uniform distribution approximation; VS-Standard achieves lowest KL divergence (0.027), demonstrating improved randomness

nodes.label: Safety Evaluation (StrongReject)
nodes.rationale: Safety assessment on 353 harmful prompts; VS maintains refusal rates >97%, confirming diversity gains do not compromise safety alignment

nodes.label: Human Study on Creative Writing Diversity
nodes.rationale: IRB-approved study with 90 annotators; inter-rater agreement (Gwet's AC1) ranges 0.54-0.87 for diversity, validating human perception of diversity improvements

nodes.label: HelpSteer Preference Dataset
nodes.author: Wang et al. (2024)
nodes.rationale: Used for Bradley-Terry regression to quantify typicality bias; α̂ = 0.57-0.65 indicates strong preference for typical responses

nodes.label: PRISM Alignment Dataset
nodes.author: Kirk et al. (2024a)
nodes.rationale: Diverse annotator pool with demographic metadata; reveals typicality bias varies by ethnicity and region, with implications for fairness

nodes.label: CoverageQA Benchmark
nodes.author: Wong et al. (2024)
nodes.rationale: Open-ended QA with multiple valid answers; used to evaluate coverage and KL divergence from pretraining distribution

nodes.label: SimpleQA Dataset

nodes.rationale: 4,326 fact-seeking questions across 10 domains; used to evaluate factual accuracy (Top@1 and Pass@N)

nodes.label: GSM8K Dataset

nodes.label: Semantic Diversity (Embedding-based)
nodes.rationale: Primary diversity metric: pairwise semantic similarity using embeddings; lower values indicate higher diversity

nodes.label: KL Divergence from Pretraining Distribution
nodes.rationale: Measures alignment with pretraining distribution; lower values indicate better representativeness

nodes.label: Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test
nodes.author: Massey (1951)
nodes.rationale: Goodness-of-fit test for distribution alignment; used in dialogue simulation to measure donation amount distribution alignment

nodes.label: Coverage-N Metric
nodes.rationale: Fraction of unique ground-truth answers generated in N samples; measures breadth of answer coverage

nodes.label: ROUGE-L Metric
nodes.author: Lin (2004)
nodes.rationale: Lexical overlap metric; lower values indicate less repetition and higher diversity in creative writing

nodes.label: Distinct-N Metric
nodes.rationale: Fraction of unique n-grams; measures lexical diversity in dialogue simulation

nodes.label: Gwet's AC1 Inter-Rater Agreement
nodes.author: Gwet (2008)
nodes.rationale: Reliability measure for human annotations; ranges 0.54-0.87 across creative writing tasks

nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
nodes.author: Christiano et al. (2017), Ouyang et al. (2022)
nodes.rationale: Standard alignment technique; paper shows RLHF amplifies typicality bias leading to mode collapse

nodes.label: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
nodes.author: Rafailov et al. (2024)
nodes.rationale: Preference optimization method; subject to same typicality bias and mode collapse as RLHF

nodes.label: Diverse Preference Optimization
nodes.author: Lanchantin et al. (2025)
nodes.rationale: Recent work on diversity in preference optimization; VS provides complementary inference-time approach

nodes.label: Decoding Strategies (Top-k, Top-p, Temperature)
nodes.author: Holtzman et al. (2020), Hewitt et al. (2022)
nodes.rationale: Standard inference-time diversity methods; VS provides more principled alternative leveraging representativeness

nodes.label: Inference-Time Scaling
nodes.author: Snell et al. (2024), Brown et al. (2024)
nodes.rationale: Repeated sampling approaches; VS offers alternative that elicits broader distribution rather than repeated sampling from single prompt

nodes.label: Synthetic Data Generation for Training
nodes.author: Ge et al. (2025), Chen et al. (2024a)
nodes.rationale: Related work on diversity in synthetic data; VS improves downstream model performance when used for finetuning

nodes.label: Computational Cost and Latency Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Major limitation: generating N candidates is more costly than single response; may constrain applicability in latency-sensitive environments

nodes.label: Dependence on Model Scale and Capability
nodes.rationale: Performance gains correlate with model scale; less capable models may lack reasoning ability to fully benefit from VS

nodes.label: Mitigating Bias in Reward Models
nodes.rationale: Future direction: address root cause of mode collapse by mitigating reward model bias through calibration and pluralistic alignment

nodes.label: Online RL with Diverse Rollouts
nodes.rationale: Future direction: apply VS to online RL to improve exploration and learning from diverse rollouts
